reason: This text fragment (Exodus 2:1-10) narrates the birth of Moses and his preservation by his mother and discovery by Pharaoh's daughter. The passage contains no depiction of violence, no reference to 'unruly people,' and no leadership model. Instead, it emphasizes compassion (Pharaoh's daughter has pity on the weeping child), care, nurturing, and practical problem-solving. The values demonstrated are protection of the vulnerable, mercy, and preservation of life—the antithesis of violence-based leadership.
